options.C: The Nigerian Medical Association Board
options.D: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: Great job! The NMCN is our guiding body. They set the rules, handle licensing, and make sure nursing standards are kept high across Nigeria.

question: How is tele-nursing different from general telemedicine?

options.A: Tele-nursing is only performed inside intensive care units
options.B: Tele-nursing focuses specifically on nursing care processes, education, and monitoring
options.C: Telemedicine can only be practiced using written letters
options.D: Telemedicine completely excludes the use of any electronic devices

explanation: Well done! While telemedicine usually centers on a doctor's medical diagnosis and treatment, tele-nursing focuses on the independent and collaborative scope of nursing care.

question: What does 'synchronous' tele-nursing communication mean?

options.A: Sending a text message that the nurse reads hours later
options.B: Real-time interaction happening simultaneously via phone or video call
options.C: Mailing a paper diary of symptoms through the postal service
options.D: Storing patient files in a locked cabinet overnight

explanation: You nailed it! Synchronous means 'at the same time'—like a live phone call or video chat where both you and the patient are actively talking right then and there.

question: A patient sends a photo of a swollen foot via WhatsApp for a nurse to check later. What type of communication is this?

options.A: Asynchronous delivery
options.B: Synchronous delivery
options.C: Direct ward admission
options.D: Emergency triage

explanation: Exactly! When you send a message or photo to be reviewed later without a live conversation happening right then, it is called asynchronous (or store-and-forward) communication.

question: How do you handle the assessment phase during a tele-nursing consultation?

options.A: By relying heavily on verbal descriptions, patient self-reports, and transmitted media
options.B: By reviewing only the physician's past medical history notes
options.C: By skipping physical checks entirely and guessing the diagnosis
options.D: By forcing every patient to travel to the central lab immediately

explanation: Good thinking! Since you can't touch the patient physically, you rely on smart questioning, listening closely, and checking photos or videos they send you.

question: Which step of the nursing process involves checking if the patient got better after your advice?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Assessment

explanation: You got it! Evaluation is our final check where we look back at our care plan to see if the patient's condition improved and if our goals were met.

question: What should you do if a patient calls reporting sudden chest pain and severe shortness of breath?

options.A: Ask them to send a text message if the pain gets worse tomorrow
options.B: Tell them to wait until next week for a routine clinic appointment
options.C: Instruct them to immediately seek emergency medical care or transport
options.D: Advise them to drink warm water and sleep for an hour

explanation: Safety first! Chest pain and severe breathing trouble are red flags. They need immediate physical medical attention, not home management.

question: Which option is NOT possible when assessing a patient during a strictly voice-only phone call?

options.A: Asking direct questions about pain level and location
options.B: Listening carefully to changes in the patient's breathing sound
options.C: Observing skin color changes directly through the phone screen
options.D: Evaluating the tone of voice and hesitation in speech

explanation: Spot on! An ordinary phone call transmits sound, not video. You can hear their breathing or tone of voice, but you cannot see if their skin is pale or jaundiced.

question: What is a major ethical worry when using tele-nursing communication?

options.A: Preventing patients from buying medications at local pharmacies
options.B: Ensuring that nurses get paid a higher salary than physicians
options.C: Maintaining patient privacy and data confidentiality over digital networks
options.D: Eliminating the need to write nursing notes in patient files

explanation: Well reasoned! Sending health info over phones or the internet can expose it to unauthorized people, making data privacy a huge ethical duty for nurses.

question: What is one of the biggest benefits of tele-nursing for patients?

options.A: Automatic provision of free smartphones to every citizen
options.B: Reduced travel time and lower transportation expenses
options.C: Guaranteed complete cure for all chronic illnesses
options.D: Elimination of all hospital fees and medicine costs

explanation: Exactly! Tele-nursing saves patients the stress, time, and money of traveling long distances just for routine check-ins or quick advice.

question: How can tele-nursing work best in rural areas with limited resources?

options.A: By requiring patients to buy expensive personal computers before getting help
options.B: By waiting until every village has advanced fibre-optic internet cables installed
options.C: By stopping all physical hospital care and replacing it with mobile apps
options.D: By utilizing simple, accessible tools like basic SMS and solar-powered communication points

explanation: You got it! Success in resource-limited settings depends on using affordable, everyday technology that fits local realities rather than waiting for fancy equipment.

question: Why is it important to teach digital health topics in nursing school?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside clinical practice with computer gaming
options.B: To prepare student nurses for modern virtual communication and digital care delivery
options.C: To ensure students never have to care for physical patients in wards
options.D: To teach students how to repair broken telephone network towers

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare is changing fast. Learning digital health early equips you with the skills you need for modern nursing practice.

question: What is the main reason we use diagnostic devices in healthcare?

options.A: To permanently cure chronic illnesses
options.B: To replace the need for physical assessments
options.C: To detect diseases and monitor health conditions
options.D: To replace human clinical judgment entirely

explanation: You've got this! Diagnostic tools simply help us gather clear facts so we can identify and track health issues. Great job starting here!

question: How should you, as a nurse, use data from a machine or diagnostic device?

options.A: Combine the machine data with patient history and physical assessment
options.B: Relies solely on the machine numbers without checking the patient
options.C: Record the numbers and discharge the patient immediately
options.D: Ignore the device data if it conflicts with a gut feeling

explanation: Machines are super helpful, but safe nursing means matching those numbers with what you actually see and hear when checking your patient!

question: What does a pulse oximeter measure in a patient?

options.A: Blood oxygen saturation levels
options.B: Electrical activity of the heart
options.C: Arterial blood pressure
options.D: Internal core body temperature

explanation: A pulse oximeter shines light through the skin to calculate how much oxygen is carried by the red blood cells. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: What should you do first if a bedside monitor shows a sudden drop in oxygen, but the patient looks calm and comfortable?

options.A: Turn off the alarm permanently so it stops annoying staff
options.B: Check the patient and the sensor placement on the finger
options.C: Call the doctor immediately to report a code blue
options.D: Assume the patient is dying and start chest compressions

explanation: Don't panic! Sensors often slip or wiggle loose. Always check your patient and the equipment first before jumping to conclusions.

question: Which imaging tool uses high-frequency sound waves instead of radiation?

options.A: PET scan
options.B: X-ray
options.C: Ultrasound
options.D: CT scan

explanation: Ultrasound relies on sound waves bouncing off internal organs to form a picture, avoiding the radiation used in X-rays and CT scans. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why is ultrasound usually chosen over X-rays when checking on a pregnant woman?

options.A: It provides clear pictures of hard bones
options.B: It requires the patient to stay still for hours
options.C: It does not use ionizing radiation
options.D: It is much cheaper than an ECG

explanation: Keeping the baby safe from radiation is a top priority during pregnancy, making ultrasound a wonderful, safe choice.

question: What safety check must you always perform before sending a patient for an MRI scan?

options.A: Excessive exposure to sun rays
options.B: Hidden metal objects and implants
options.C: Low levels of vitamin C
options.D: A history of drinking cold water

explanation: MRI machines use super strong magnets! Checking for metal keeps patients safe from flying objects or damaged implants like pacemakers.

question: In a busy emergency accident unit, why would a doctor order a CT scan instead of an MRI?

options.A: CT scans use harmless sound waves only
options.B: CT scans are typically much faster to perform
options.C: CT scans require no electricity to run
options.D: CT scans do not use any form of radiation

explanation: When every second counts in emergency care, CT scans deliver quick pictures of the brain or chest in just minutes.

question: In hospital tech talk, what does PACS stand for?

options.A: Picture Archiving and Communication System
options.B: Patient Assessment and Clinical Sign system
options.C: Primary Acute Care Support network
options.D: Portable Automated Clinical Scanner

explanation: PACS is simply the digital filing cabinet hospitals use to store and share medical images safely.

question: Why is it so helpful to link diagnostic results directly into the Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever seeing their own medical information
options.B: It automatically cures the patient without requiring nurse intervention
options.C: It stops diagnostic machines from breaking down over time
options.D: It allows healthcare providers to view test results and images in one central place

explanation: Having everything in one digital spot helps the whole care team make quick, safe decisions without chasing paper files!

question: Which of these choices is a MAJOR safety violation when handling hospital equipment?

options.A: Checking for frayed electrical cords
options.B: Obtaining informed consent from the patient
options.C: Skipping equipment cleaning to save time
options.D: Ensuring proper disinfection between patients

explanation: Never skip cleaning! Proper maintenance and disinfection protect patients from nasty infections and keep equipment running smoothly.

question: Why must reusable tools like ultrasound probes be carefully disinfected after every single patient?

options.A: To prevent the spread of hospital-acquired infections
options.B: To make the machine look brand new to the patient
options.C: To improve the clarity of the computer images
options.D: To ensure the battery stays fully charged

explanation: Wiping down equipment stops germs from hitching a ride from one patient to the next. You're building great clinical habits!

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring devices in nursing informatics?

options.A: To completely replace the need for physical nursing assessments
options.B: To automatically track patient physiological status in real time
options.C: To manually calculate monthly hospital billing statements
options.D: To serve as a decorative fixture at the hospital bedside

explanation: Monitoring devices are designed to continuously track vital signs and physiological data without requiring constant manual input. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h1)

question: How do monitoring devices improve nursing documentation?

options.A: By transmitting captured data directly into electronic health records
options.B: By erasing old vital signs every twelve hours
options.C: By forcing nurses to write everything on paper charts first
options.D: By locking all patient data so other staff cannot read it

explanation: Connecting bedside devices to digital records cuts down on manual entry mistakes and saves time. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h1)

question: What does a pulse oximeter actually measure in the patient?

options.A: Exact blood pressure inside the artery
options.B: Total red blood cell count in the body
options.C: Oxygen saturation percentage in the blood
options.D: Carbon dioxide levels in the lungs

explanation: The device uses light absorption to estimate how much hemoglobin is carrying oxygen. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h2)

question: A patient's pulse oximeter shows 82%, but they are talking and breathing easily. What should you do first?

options.A: Turn off the monitor because it is definitely broken
options.B: Immediately start chest compressions and call a code blue
options.C: Check the physical patient and look for cold fingers or nail polish
options.D: Assume the patient is in severe respiratory distress

explanation: Always assess your patient before the machine! Poor circulation or dark nail polish often causes false low readings. Great nursing instinct!

question: What is the main purpose of placing electrode pads on a patient's chest for cardiac monitoring?

options.A: To capture the electrical activity and heart rhythm
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the heart muscle
options.C: To keep the patient warm during cold hospital nights
options.D: To deliver mild electric shocks to warm the skin

explanation: Electrodes pick up the heart's electrical impulses and display them as a waveform on the screen. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is alarm fatigue a dangerous issue with continuous cardiac monitors?

options.A: The monitor stops working after a certain number of alarms
options.B: Staff may ignore or turn down alarms because of too many false warnings
options.C: The batteries in the monitor run out of power too quickly
options.D: Patients get too tired from hearing the screen beep all day

explanation: Constant ringing from non-urgent alerts can cause nurses to miss a real emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h3)

question: What do clinical decision support systems do with data from monitoring devices?

options.A: Automatically discharge patients when vital signs are normal
options.B: Print paper reports for the hospital marketing department
options.C: Analyze trends to alert the care team about potential problems
options.D: Hide bad vital signs so the patient stays calm

explanation: CDS software looks at patient data streams to spot worsening trends early. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h4)

question: How does data integration help prevent patient emergencies?

options.A: By sending text messages directly to the patient's family members
options.B: By combining multiple vital signs to catch subtle signs of decline early
options.C: By stopping nurses from having to check vital signs manually ever again
options.D: By letting machines make all medical diagnoses without human help

explanation: Looking at combined trends helps nurses intervene before a minor issue becomes a major emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical concern when using connected monitoring devices?

options.A: Balancing constant safety tracking with the right to privacy
options.B: Guarantees that patient medical bills will always be cheaper
options.C: Making sure patients understand and consent to surveillance
options.D: Protecting wireless patient data from cyber security threats

explanation: Monitoring devices do not guarantee lower bills; privacy, security, and consent are the true ethical concerns. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why must nurses be careful about continuous patient surveillance in clinical spaces?

options.A: Doctors are not legally allowed to look at video feeds
options.B: Cameras use up too much electricity in the hospital room
options.C: It can make patients feel vulnerable and invade their privacy
options.D: Patients will stop sleeping and watch the cameras all night

explanation: Constant monitoring can compromise personal dignity if not balanced carefully with patient comfort and consent. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is direct nursing delivery technology mainly used for?

options.A: Ordering bulk kitchen supplies for the cafeteria
options.B: Managing hospital billing and staff payroll records
options.C: Scheduling yearly maintenance for the facility generator
options.D: Assisting hands-on patient care at the bedside

explanation: Spot on! These tools are built specifically to help you interact directly with patients and deliver hands-on care safely.

question: Why is it important for modern nurses to get comfortable using bedside technology?

options.A: It shapes every shift and helps protect patients from human error
options.B: Patients refuse care unless digital devices are present
options.C: It completely replaces the need to perform physical assessments
options.D: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on computer typing speed

explanation: You got it! Smart tools are part of daily clinical life, and they act as a safety net to catch mistakes before they hurt anyone.

question: During Barcode Medication Administration (BCMA), what are the three main things you scan?

options.A: Nurse badge, patient wristband, and medication package
options.B: Dietary tray card, patient chart, and nurse uniform
options.C: Hospital logo, lab tube sticker, and bed frame barcode
options.D: Doctor license, room door number, and IV bag label

explanation: Brilliant! Scanning the nurse, the patient, and the drug is your golden rule to make sure the right meds reach the right person.

question: Why is it risky to blindly trust BCMA without double-checking things yourself?

options.A: Scanners often delete medication orders randomly during night shifts
options.B: It cannot catch errors made during pharmacy compounding or doctor entry
options.C: Computers cannot read barcodes if the patient is sleeping
options.D: It prevents nurses from checking patient vital signs manually

explanation: Exactly right. The scanner only reads what was typed into the system. If the original prescription was wrong, the scanner might still green-light it!

question: What happens when an IV pump triggers a 'hard stop'?

options.A: The machine automatically recalculates the correct weight-based dose
options.B: The pump completely blocks the rate and prevents starting the infusion
options.C: The pharmacy is notified to send a replacement pump immediately
options.D: An alarm sounds loudly until the patient presses a bedside button

explanation: Spot on! A hard stop sets an unbreakable safety boundary so you don't accidentally infuse an unsafe dose.

question: What is the main safety perk of having a drug library built into a smart IV pump?

options.A: It alerts nurses when a dose falls outside safe clinical limits
options.B: It automatically orders new IV bags when fluid levels run low
options.C: It replaces the need to check patient IV insertion sites
options.D: It measures the exact urine output generated during the shift

explanation: You nailed it! The drug library acts like a safety checklist, warning you instantly if a programmed dose is too high or too low.

question: In a busy clinical ward, what do we mean by 'alarm fatigue'?

options.A: A patient's inability to sleep because of noisy hospital equipment
options.B: Becoming desensitized to constant monitor beeps and ignoring them
options.C: Physical exhaustion caused by carrying mobile alert devices
options.D: The battery drain that happens when monitors run all night

explanation: Correct! When alarms go off constantly for minor things, staff get tired of the noise and might accidentally miss a real emergency.

question: How do smart beds help keep vulnerable hospital patients safe?

options.A: They automatically administer pain medication when turning
options.B: They replace the need for physical therapists on surgical wards
options.C: Built-in scales eliminate the need to chart daily fluid intake
options.D: Sensors alert staff when an unassisted patient tries to stand up

explanation: Brilliant! Smart bed exit alarms give you a quick heads-up so you can rush over and prevent a nasty fall.

question: What is a major danger when nurses take shortcuts ('workarounds') around safety tech?

options.A: The hospital computer system automatically deletes their nursing license
options.B: It defeats the safety safeguards and increases the risk of patient harm
options.C: Patients will complain about the slow speed of the nursing staff
options.D: The pharmacy department will refuse to dispense any more medications

explanation: Spot on! Bypassing safety prompts removes the digital barrier that was put there specifically to protect your patient from human error.

question: A busy nurse decides to scan a patient's barcode taped to the computer instead of walking to the bedside to scan the wristband. What is this an example of?

options.A: Standard hospital protocol for rushed shifts
options.B: A dangerous clinical workaround
options.C: Proper use of bedside mobile technology
options.D: An efficient time-saving strategy

explanation: You got it! Scanning away from the bedside defeats the whole point of identity checks and opens the door to a wrong-patient medication error.

question: Which of these commonly causes frustration when using mobile nursing technology on the ward?

options.A: Too many physical stairs in modern multi-story hospitals
options.B: Dead batteries and poor wireless internet connectivity
options.C: Patients demanding to program the IV pumps themselves
options.D: Doctors refusing to let nurses touch computer carts

explanation: So true! Nothing slows down a shift quite like a dying battery or a spinning loading wheel when you're trying to chart quickly.

question: Why is poor staff training during a new technology rollout so dangerous?

options.A: It forces the hospital to close its emergency department
options.B: It makes patients lose trust in the hospital cleaning staff
options.C: It causes hospital computers to catch computer viruses
options.D: It leads to confusion, frustration, and dangerous workarounds

explanation: Exactly! If nurses aren't properly trained on new equipment, stress takes over under pressure, leading to risky shortcuts.

question: What is one exciting benefit expected from future voice-activated documentation tools?

options.A: Allowing nurses to speak clinical notes while performing procedures
options.B: Replacing the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: Automatically bathing patients using robotic spray systems
options.D: Eliminating all hospital noise during the night shift

explanation: Brilliant! Voice tech aims to save us time by letting us dictate our notes hands-free while we work.

question: No matter how advanced hospital technology gets, what will always remain the nurse's primary challenge?

options.A: Balancing machine intelligence with compassionate human care
options.B: Finding enough electrical outlets to charge wearable patches
options.C: Convincing hospital administrators to buy cheaper equipment
options.D: Learning how to repair broken computer microchips

explanation: Spot on! Machines can crunch numbers and track drips, but nursing fundamentally depends on your human empathy, touch, and critical thinking.

question: What is the main goal of using patient assistive devices in healthcare?

options.A: To increase the cost of long-term care stays
options.B: To help patients maintain independence and safety
options.C: To reduce hospital administration paperwork
options.D: To completely replace the need for nursing staff

explanation: You got this! Assistive devices are designed to empower patients, helping them move and care for themselves safely and with dignity.

question: Which of these is considered a simple, low-tech assistive device?

options.A: A computerized communication board
options.B: A manual reacher
options.C: A motorized wheelchair
options.D: A robotic rehabilitation suit

explanation: Great job! Low-tech devices are simple tools that don't need electricity or fancy computer chips to work.

question: Which tool is best for sliding an immobile patient smoothly across the bed sheet?

options.A: A motorized wheelchair
options.B: Slide sheets
options.C: A mechanical lift
options.D: A gait belt

explanation: Spot on! Slide sheets cut down friction against the mattress, making it so much easier and safer to reposition patients without hurting their skin or your back.

question: A weak patient is learning to walk down the hallway and needs a little extra support to stay steady. What should you use?

options.A: A mechanical hoist
options.B: A slide sheet
options.C: A ceiling lift
options.D: A gait belt

explanation: You're doing great! A gait belt goes snugly around the patient's waist, giving you a safe and secure grip to steady them as they walk.

question: How can a patient with severe upper body paralysis steer an automated wheelchair?

options.A: A heavy floor-based foot pedal
options.B: A sip-and-puff mechanism
options.C: A ceiling-mounted pull cord
options.D: A standard manual push rim

explanation: Brilliant! A sip-and-puff control lets patients steer simply by blowing into or inhaling through a small straw tube using breath pressure.

question: Why do you need to work with an occupational therapist before a patient gets an automated wheelchair?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost for hospital billing
options.B: To ensure the wheelchair matches the room color scheme
options.C: To train the nursing staff on physical lifting techniques
options.D: To evaluate if the patient has the cognitive and motor skills to steer safely

explanation: Exactly right! We need to make sure the patient can safely control the powered chair so they don't accidentally run into walls or hurt anyone.

question: How do robotic exoskeletons help patients recovering from a spinal injury or stroke?

options.A: By replacing the need for any physical therapy supervision
options.B: By automatically administering intravenous medications
options.C: By permanently curing all forms of neurological paralysis
options.D: By guiding their legs through repetitive walking movements to promote recovery

explanation: Wonderful! Exoskeletons help by moving the legs through steady, repeated steps, which helps retrain the brain and spinal pathways.

question: What is one major limitation of using robots in patient care units?

options.A: Robots require continuous physical lifting from bedside nurses
options.B: Robots lack clinical intuition and cannot interpret subtle human emotional cues
options.C: Robots completely eliminate the need for electronic health records
options.D: Robots are incapable of moving along hospital corridors

explanation: Spot on! Machines follow strict programming. They can never fully replace the warm, empathetic touch and observant eye of a real nurse.

question: What is the most important factor when checking if a patient is ready for a high-tech mobility device?

options.A: The current market price of the technology
options.B: The brand name of the device manufacturer
options.C: The patient's cognitive status and judgment
options.D: The color preference of the patient's family

explanation: You got it! A patient's thinking ability and good judgment are key to making sure they can use high-tech gear safely.

question: You are discharging a patient with a new motorized wheelchair. What is a key safety step you must take?

options.A: Teach the patient and family proper usage, charging habits, and safety checks
options.B: Instruct the patient never to use the wheelchair outside of the house
options.C: Disable the emergency braking system to make the ride smoother
options.D: Hide the charging cables so the patient cannot plug the chair in

explanation: Brilliant! Patient education prevents accidents at home and ensures they know how to take care of their equipment.

question: What is a common ethical worry when patients use modern smart assistive devices?

options.A: Loss of personal privacy through continuous health data collection
options.B: Excessive face-to-face interaction with hospital staff
options.C: Immediate destruction of all electronic health records
options.D: Uncontrolled increases in physical nursing workloads

explanation: Correct! Smart devices often track daily movements and health stats, which raises real questions about keeping patient data private.

question: Why can relying too much on assistive technology become a problem in patient care?

options.A: It can reduce human interaction and lead to patient isolation
options.B: It automatically cures all chronic illnesses within days
options.C: It forces patients to perform rigorous physical exercises
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medical research

explanation: You're doing great! While tech is helpful, leaning on machines too much can cut down on the warm, meaningful human contact patients need.

question: What is the primary purpose of indirect nursing care technologies?

options.A: To support behind-the-scenes hospital operations and administrative tasks
options.B: To monitor patient vital signs directly at the skin surface
options.C: To replace bedside nurses during surgical procedures
options.D: To diagnose complex diseases without laboratory tests

explanation: Indirect care technologies handle logistics, scheduling, and inventory so that nurses spend less time on paperwork. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: How do indirect care technologies ultimately benefit patients?

options.A: By removing all chances of medical errors happening
options.B: By allowing nurses to spend more time on direct patient care
options.C: By lowering the financial cost of hospital building construction
options.D: By completely eliminating the need for human nurses

explanation: Automating administrative duties frees up nurses to focus on direct patient assessment and treatment. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: How do RFID tags help clinical staff manage equipment?

options.A: By diagnosing equipment mechanical failures before they happen
options.B: By allowing rapid tracking and location of mobile medical devices
options.C: By cleaning and sterilizing surgical instruments automatically
options.D: By measuring the exact battery life of infusion pumps

explanation: RFID tags emit radio signals that let staff pinpoint the exact location of valuable mobile hospital equipment. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h2)

question: A maternity ward wants to stop unauthorized movement of newborns. Which technology is most useful?

options.A: Barcoded medication carts
options.B: Electronic spreadsheets
options.C: Automated staffing rosters
options.D: RFID security bands

explanation: RFID bands worn by newborns trigger alarms if they pass through designated exit doors without authorization. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h2)

question: What happens when stock levels drop below a safe minimum in an electronic inventory system?

options.A: An automatic reorder alert is generated
options.B: The hospital power generator shuts down automatically
options.C: All patient charts are locked until new stock arrives
options.D: The nursing supervisor's license is suspended

explanation: Electronic systems track thresholds and notify purchasing staff to reorder items before they run out completely. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is manual inventory tracking discouraged in busy hospital wards?

options.A: It uses too much electricity compared to digital systems
options.B: It makes medical equipment too heavy to push around
options.C: It stops doctors from writing paper prescriptions
options.D: It is prone to human error and wastes valuable nursing time

explanation: Manual counting takes nurses away from patient care and frequently results in unexpected stockouts. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the main function of a computerized staffing system?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial salary of every hospital worker
options.B: To track the expiration dates of intravenous fluids in the pharmacy
options.C: To monitor patient vital signs remotely from a central nursing station
options.D: To generate balanced work schedules based on patient needs and staff skills

explanation: Staffing software matches patient census data and nurse competencies to create safe shift rosters. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which statement best describes the role of nurse managers when using scheduling software?

options.A: They have no control over the roster once the computer generates it
options.B: They are only responsible for entering patient billing data into the system
options.C: They stop working night shifts completely because software handles them
options.D: They must still review and adjust schedules for human factors and emergencies

explanation: Software assists with the math, but nurse managers must use clinical judgment for unexpected personal situations. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why is system integration important for hospital technology tools?

options.A: It lowers the physical weight of computer monitors at the nursing station
options.B: It removes the need for any internet connection in the hospital
options.C: It allows separate digital tools to share data and work together smoothly
options.D: It forces all patients to use mobile phones for their medical records

explanation: Integration connects isolated systems so information flows freely between inventory, staffing, and patient care records. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h5)

question: A Nigerian hospital installs new software that does not connect with existing supply records, causing extra paperwork. What is lacking?

options.A: Strict punitive measures against nurses who make mistakes
options.B: Longer working hours for administrative staff members
options.C: Proper workflow optimization and system integration
options.D: A higher number of surgical operations performed daily

explanation: When technology is not integrated well into workflows, it creates bottlenecks and extra administrative burdens. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge when adopting hospital technology in resource-constrained settings?

options.A: Resistance to change from staff used to paper records
options.B: Unstable electricity and power supply disruptions
